item.title: Wheat breeder loses faith in Canada’s system
item.description: Richard Cuthbert, a former AAFC wheat breeder in Swift Current, resigned from his job in January because he believed he could “no longer be productive.”

item.title: Canada needs an agriculture strategy to rebuild trust with producers, investors and trade partners: report
item.description: Canada needs a national agriculture strategy with clear priorities and results according to a new report from the Canada West Foundation.

item.title: Increased demand only way out of supply glut
item.description: Grain markets are still suffering from a supply glut. The only way out of it is to increase demand, says the USDA’s chief economist.

item.title: Trump declares 10 per cent global tariff after Supreme Court decision
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court struck down on Friday President Donald Trump’s sweeping tariffs that he pursued under a law meant for use in national emergencies.

item.title: U.S. Supreme Court rejects Trump’s global tariffs
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court struck down on Friday President Donald Trump’s sweeping tariffs that he pursued under a law meant for use in national emergencies.

item.title: OPINION: Draining wetlands produces substantial emissions in the Canadian Prairies
item.description: While wetlands sequester carbon, they also naturally release greenhouse gases (GHG) into the atmosphere. Our new study has found that widespread wetland drainage on Prairie farmland releases 2.1 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (CO₂-eq) per year.

item.title: Feed Grains Weekly: Domestic prices remain flat
item.description: Although there has been some upward movement in feed grain prices, particularly in Alberta, it’s not domestic demand that’s pushing them higher, said Jim Beusekom, president of Market Place Commodities in Lethbridge on Feb. 19.

item.title: USDA defends $12 billion subsidy amid farm economy challenges
item.description: As the U.S. Department of Agriculture prepares to dole out $12 billion (C$16.4 billion) in government subsidies next week, officials and economists at the agency’s annual forum near Washington defended the assistance as a necessary measure to prevent more farmers from financial ruin.

item.title: U.S. trade rep credits Trump for ‘paradigm shift’
item.description: USTR chief agriculture negotiator says Trump has transformed trade negotiations with a goal of turning a trade deficit into a surplus.
